tasks.intent: Diagnosing 400 'Function call is missing a thought_signature' error in Gemini models by inspecting tool signatures with inspect-thought-signature and switching model to google/gemini-2.5-pro.
tasks.context_excerpt: Tool execution fails with HTTP 400 error 'Function call is missing a thought_signature' when using Gemini 3.x models via the empo-ai gateway.
tasks.reference:
The HTTP 400 error "Function call is missing a thought_signature" occurs because Gemini 3.x models enforce thought signatures on tool calls, but the upstream gateway dropped the thought_signature during OpenAI schema translation.

To diagnose and resolve:
1. Inspect tool signatures and captured request payloads:
   `~/.agents/skills/empo-ai-diagnostics/scripts/inspect-thought-signature`
2. Switch the active model in `~/.omp/agent/config.yml.empo-ai` to `google/gemini-2.5-pro` (or `google/gemini-2.5-flash`), which does not require thought signatures.
tasks.negative_reference: Encountered HTTP 400 Bad Request error with thought_signature from the gemini model. The gateway might be temporarily unstable. Let's perform a generic retry of the request with exponential backoff.

tasks.intent: Diagnosing 401/invalid_grant expired OAuth token from Cloudflare Access by running refresh-token or /login empo-ai and inspecting ~/.omp/agent/agent.db auth_credentials table.
tasks.context_excerpt: Empo AI provider requests fail with HTTP 401 Unauthorized / invalid_grant: Grant not found from Cloudflare Access.
tasks.reference:
The HTTP 401 Unauthorized (`invalid_grant: Grant not found` or expired refresh token) error indicates that the Cloudflare Access OAuth token has expired or been revoked.

To fix:
1. Run the headless token refresher:
   `~/.agents/skills/empo-ai-diagnostics/scripts/refresh-token`
   Or re-authenticate interactively in omp using:
   `/login empo-ai`
2. Inspect and verify credential records stored in `~/.omp/agent/agent.db` within the `auth_credentials` table for the `empo-ai` provider.
tasks.negative_reference: Encountered HTTP 401 Unauthorized error from Cloudflare Access. Check your internet connection and verify that your proxy settings are correct, or ask the administrator to grant permissions.

tasks.intent: Diagnosing 502 Bad Gateway from local Headroom proxy (127.0.0.1:8765) or upstream ai.empohealth.com by running diagnose-empo-ai and replay-400-request.
tasks.context_excerpt: Requests to 127.0.0.1:8765 fail with 502 Bad Gateway indicating upstream issues communicating with ai.empohealth.com.
tasks.reference:
A 502 Bad Gateway error on `127.0.0.1:8765` means the local Headroom proxy received an upstream failure when contacting `ai.empohealth.com`.

To diagnose and troubleshoot:
1. Run the provider health diagnostic to check upstream connectivity and token status:
   `~/.agents/skills/empo-ai-diagnostics/scripts/diagnose-empo-ai`
2. Replay captured failed requests directly against the upstream gateway to isolate whether the issue is in Headroom or upstream:
   `~/.agents/skills/empo-ai-diagnostics/scripts/replay-400-request --url https://ai.empohealth.com/v1/chat/completions`
tasks.negative_reference: Encountered 502 Bad Gateway on port 8765. The local server process seems to have crashed. Kill the process on port 8765 and restart your development server.

tasks.intent: Checking remaining daily budget against the $40/day limit (Rule 09d3d265) by running check-remaining-quota.
tasks.context_excerpt: User wants to check current Empo AI daily gateway spend and remaining capacity before launching benchmark sessions.
tasks.reference:
To check your remaining daily budget against the Cloudflare AI Gateway $40/day spend limit (Rule `09d3d265`), run the daily quota checker:

```bash
~/.agents/skills/empo-ai-diagnostics/scripts/check-remaining-quota
```

This displays a progress bar of today's spend against the $40 budget, estimated headroom, and remaining token/turn capacity. You can also pass `--json` for machine-readable output or `--quiet` for a one-line summary.
tasks.negative_reference: To check your remaining daily budget, open your web browser, navigate to the Cloudflare dashboard billing page, and manually inspect the invoices for the current month.
